Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.withHeader` method takes an array of header strings and creates a new `CSVFormat` object with the specified headers.

Given the failing test, it seems that the issue is related to handling empty header names in Excel files, resulting in an `IllegalArgumentException` with a message indicating a duplicate name of "". The problem occurs during the initialization of the header in the `CSVParser`.

Based on the provided code snippet from the `CSVParser.parse` method, it directly initializes the `CSVParser` with the given format and the input string. The `CSVFormat.EXCEL.withHeader()` method is used to set the format with headers.

To fix the issue of ignoring empty header names and prevent the `IllegalArgumentException`, the initialization logic in the `CSVParser` class should be updated to handle empty header names appropriately.

Possible Fix:
```java
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVParser.initializeHeader(java.util.List<java.lang.String>, boolean)
```

This method can be modified to handle empty header names properly, ensuring that the headers are initialized correctly without causing duplicate name issues when empty names are present in Excel files.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
